text:
emily.ng: Hi all — weird one. Had a teletherapy session last week, provider billed the claim under my spouse's name by mistake. They already sent an EOB to the spouse and the claim was denied/processed wrong. I need to get this fixed and make sure cost shares go to my account, not theirs. Any steps?

rafael.benefits: Sorry that happened, emily. Short version: ask the provider to void/re-submit the claim with the correct subscriber name and member ID (your Redwood plan subscriber), and request a corrected EOB from the payer. Provider needs to include the correct patient relationship, subscriber ID, and possibly a corrected claim form (CMS-1500 or UB-04). :thumbsup:

emily.ng: Appreciate it. Do you have a short template I can send to the clinic billing team? They sound flustered.

rafael.benefits: Yep — below is a quick provider template you can paste/send. Also attach a photo of your digital ID card and note the correct member ID and DOB. If the payer rejects, escalate to benefits@redwood.com and tag us.

benefits-bot: FYI — standard turnaround for corrected claim processing is ~30-45 days after payer receives corrected claim. If it's time-sensitive (balance notice) ask the provider to flag it as "billing error needing urgent adjustment."

emily.ng: Posting the template I sent so others can reuse. cc @maria.finance in case any billing holds hit payroll.

rafael.benefits: Sample provider message (copy/paste):

```
To: [Clinic Billing]
Subject: Request to Void and Re-submit Claim — Incorrect Subscriber Name

Hello,

Patient: Emily Ng (date of birth: 1990-06-12)
Service Date: 2026-03-10
Original Claim ID: 1234567890

We were notified that the claim for services on the date above was billed under the incorrect subscriber name (Jane Ng). Please void the original claim and resubmit a corrected claim to the insurer with the following subscriber information:

Subscriber name: Emily Ng
Subscriber ID: RWD-000123456
Insurance carrier: Redwood Inference Benefits Plan (Group: REDWOOD-01)
Patient relationship to subscriber: Self
Provider NPI: [enter NPI]
Tax ID / TIN: [enter if requested]

Additionally, please request a corrected EOB from the payer and provide a copy to the patient once available. If the payer requires an authorization or supporting documentation, please contact me at emily.ng@example.com or call me at (555) 555-0123.

Thank you,
Emily Ng
```

anil.hr: That template is solid. Two operational notes: 1) If the provider says they can only submit an appeal instead, have them include a statement that the billed subscriber was incorrect and provide documentation (copy of member ID + signed statement). 2) If the provider wants to bill under spouse temporarily to avoid collections, ask them to add a note "awaiting corrected claim/appeal" and give you 14 days before any external collections.

maria.finance: If a vendor posts a balance that ends up being our responsibility to reimburse (rare), please save all receipts — finance can process reimbursement to the employee but we need the corrected EOB that shows the payment adjustment. Send to finance-ops@redwood.com with the corrected EOB and provider invoice.

emily.ng: Clinic replied and asked for a signed authorization to share PHI with me (they inadvertently used spouse's portal). Is there a standard form or wording?

rafael.benefits: Use this quick PHI release line inside the message or an email signed by the subscriber — that's usually enough for billing teams: "I, Emily Ng (DOB 1990-06-12), authorize [Clinic Name] to share billing and claim information with me and to submit corrected claims to my insurer on my behalf." If they need a signature, sign and date it and attach a photo of your ID card.

emily.ng: They also asked for the spouse's consent to void — spouse is fine with it but can't come into clinic. Can spouse just email?

anil.hr: Yes, spouse email OK as long as it contains subscriber/spouse name, DOB, claim ID, and an explicit line like "I, Jane Ng, authorize [Clinic Name] to void the claim submitted under my name and allow resubmission under Emily Ng (Subscriber ID RWD-000123456)." Have them include date and e-signature line.

benefits-bot: Checklist for emily: 1) Send provider template + photo of your digital ID card. 2) Sign PHI release if requested. 3) Ask provider to void original claim and resubmit with correct subscriber. 4) Request corrected EOB from payer and ask provider to email it to you + benefits@redwood.com. 5) If provider threatens collections, cc benefits@redwood.com and anil.hr.

emily.ng: Wonderful — following up now. Will post updates. Thanks all :heart:

rafael.benefits: Happy to help. Ping if they stall and we can do an outreach to the payer rep.
